title: Tree diagrams and tables of outcomes
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:20Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point, mat-listing-outcomes-compound-events, teaches the same listing of outcomes with trees and tables, but it also teaches finding probabilities and its second question tests that, which goes beyond this point's brief, so a new point is the safer match.

draft.title: Tree diagrams and tables of outcomes
card: A multistage experiment has two or more steps, such as tossing a coin and then rolling a die. A list of every possible result is called the sample space.
Each step is a set of branches. Follow each path from left to right to list one outcome. Tossing a coin then a die gives H1, H2, H3, H4, H5, H6, T1, T2, T3, T4, T5 and T6.
For two steps, put the results of step 1 down the side and step 2 along the top. Each cell is one outcome.
Count the outcomes by multiplying. A coin has 2 results and a die has 6, so there are \(2 \times 6 = 12\) outcomes. Three steps work the same way: multiply all three counts.
draft.remember: List every path or cell so no outcome is missed. The number of outcomes is the product of the results at each step.

a.q: A spinner has 3 equal sections: red, blue and green. It is spun and then a coin is tossed. How many outcomes are in the sample space?
a.why: The spinner has 3 results and the coin has 2, so there are \(3 \times 2 = 6\) outcomes. Adding gives 5, but each spinner result can pair with both coin results, so the counts are multiplied.
a.clue: Each spinner result pairs with every coin result.

b.q: Lena tosses a coin three times and lists the outcomes with a tree diagram. How many outcomes have exactly two heads?
b.why: There are \(2 \times 2 \times 2 = 8\) outcomes in total. The ones with exactly two heads are HHT, HTH and THH, which is 3. The number 8 is the whole sample space, not just the outcomes with two heads.
b.clue: List all the paths, then pick out those with two H.

wants.brief: A tree diagram for tossing a coin then rolling a die. Two first branches labelled H and T. From each, six branches labelled 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. The end of each path is labelled with its outcome, such as H1 and T6.
wants.why: It shows how each path gives one outcome and how the branches spread out.
